purpose: Explore whether Atlas geometry helps predict binding-site locations, using fixed, explicit visual alignment.
layout: DNA observations and the selected Atlas geometry share one graph in all three views.
data_mapping: Original experiment-v1 interval mappings are unchanged.

atlas_registration.beta: Original nine-position residue grid: turn = residue / 9; path starts at 4.
atlas_registration.full_circle: One complete DNA window occupies one turn; both layers start at north and run clockwise.
atlas_registration.line: Unwrap the same Atlas turns: guide_offset = turn * window_length_bp. Connecting curves show the Atlas path; they are not DNA measurements.
atlas_registration.m9: DNA anchors use residue / 9 turns; each Atlas guide retains its native 9- or 24-position grid. Angular alignment does not equate a period index with a residue value.

display.m9_dot_area: Area is proportional to observation count: radius = 19 * sqrt(count / maximum_count_in_current_selection), in SVG units.
display.zero_count: Small grey grid point; no filled observation disc.
display.density_bin_units: Equal DNA-coordinate sections; bins count interval centres and are a display choice.
display.circle_density: Outward bar length is proportional to bin count, scaled within the current selection.
display.selection: White outlines identify the selected observation or its M9 node.
display.atlas_path: Coloured paths retain Atlas geometry; they do not represent measured movement or a temporal binding sequence.

assessment: Visual exploration. No positional tolerance, association statistic, matched-control test or biological prediction accuracy has been evaluated.
